title: How the ‘luteal uglies’ impact women during their periods
description:
Across social media young women are discussing the "luteal uglies." These are changes in appearance and mood that women experience during the luteal phase of their menstrual cycle. We hear from women in Vietnam, the Philippines, and the UK about the symptoms they experience, from acne and bloating to fatigue and brain fog.

But what’s behind these changes? Dr Helen O'Neill, an associate professor in reproductive and molecular genetics at University College London, explains how changing hormone levels impact women’s bodies and their brains. She also offers some tips and coping strategies.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討社群媒體上熱議的 luteal uglies 現象，即女性在經前黃體期面臨的身心變化。節目聽取來自加拿大、越南、菲律賓與英國女性的親身經歷，包含痘痘、腹脹、體重增加 1 至 1.5 公斤、疲勞、情緒波動與腦霧等症狀。倫敦大學學院 UCL 生殖與分子遺傳學副教授 Helen O'Neill 博士解釋，排卵後雌激素與黃體素濃度的急劇下降，會增加皮脂分泌並影響血清素與大腦功能，進而導致皮膚惡化與情緒低落。對此， O'Neill 博士建議女性透過追蹤月經週期、維持適度運動、改善睡眠衛生與避免飲酒來應對，同時鼓勵男性主動了解女性生理週期，給予身邊女性更多支持。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, presenter Hannah Gelbart explores the viral trend known as the "luteal uglies"—the physical and emotional changes women experience during the luteal phase preceding their periods. Women from Canada, Vietnam, the Philippines, and the UK share symptoms such as acne, bloating, water weight gain, fatigue, brain fog, and mood swings. Dr. Helen O'Neill, an associate professor at University College London, explains that a rapid drop in estrogen and progesterone after ovulation alters skin oil production, serotonin support, and brain function. Dr. O'Neill advises against bad social media tips and offers practical coping strategies, including tracking menstrual cycles, maintaining moderate exercise, practicing good sleep hygiene, and avoiding alcohol. She also encourages men to educate themselves about the menstrual cycle to better support the women in their lives.
